Event display

eventdisplay shows one physics event in one figure. It takes the time of the event, or a row of its event tier:

l200 = LegendData(:l200)
evts = read_ldata(l200, :jlevt, filekey)

eventdisplay(l200, evts.tstart[i])   # reads only the row of the event
eventdisplay(l200, evts[i])

The time must be the exact tstart of the event: a time without a row is an error, and a DateTime is not accepted because its millisecond resolution cannot match tstart. lplot(l200, evts[i]) and lplot(l200, DataTier(:jlevt), evts.tstart[i]) give the same figures.

The display supports physics (phy) events only. An event without a triggered HPGe detector, or a row without the columns tstart, geds, spms, ged_spm and ged_pmt, throws an ArgumentError. The display needs:

  • the metadata hardware/geometry, with the position of every HPGe detector and SiPM;
  • the lar_cut section of the SiPM event configuration, with the windows, the spm_windows, the energy_types with their pos and is_dc, and the cuts. A cut named all is required: its window is the time axis of the SiPM triggers and the window of the LAr PE sum and multiplicity.

The array, the events and the waveforms on this page are made up. The file docs/src/recipes/event_display_data.jl writes them into a copy of the metadata of LegendTestData, and evts holds two event rows.

using CairoMakie, LegendMakie

An event

eventdisplay(l200, evts[1])

The figure shows:

  • Title row: the file key, the date and time of the event in UTC, and the logo.
  • Top view: the HPGe strings and the SiPM modules, with the triggered strings in orange. A SiPM module with light takes the color of its photoelectrons, added up over the module. The shaded sector is the geometric LAr cut around the triggered strings, and a blue edge marks a SiPM inside it.
  • SiPM triggers: below the top view, a bar per SiPM trigger at its time relative to the HPGe t0, in the color of its photoelectrons, over the windows of the LAr cut. Triggers that the cut flags as dark counts are left out.
  • Side view: the array unrolled around its axis. The horizontal axis is the azimuth relative to the triggered string with the largest energy, so no string hides another one. A white rectangle is a detector that the event does not hold, usually one that is switched off.
  • Observables: the energy sum and the light of the event, its cuts, and one row per triggered HPGe detector.
  • Waveforms: the waveforms of lplot(data, ts), with the HPGe t0 as a vertical line and the windows of the LAr cut as bands in the SiPM panel.

The table reads its cuts from the event tier. true in a column means passed:

RowColumnMeaning
LAr cutged_spm.is_valid_larThe decision of the production. It does not change with the keyword lar_cut.
muon cutged_pmt.is_valid_muonNo flagged PMT event in the time window around the HPGe t0. Also passed when the event has no PMT event.
QCgeds.is_valid_qcEvery HPGe channel of the event, not only the triggered ones, is an empty trace, a single pulse or cross-talk.
PSD cutgeds.is_valid_psdThe triggered HPGe detectors, with the classifier of the production, which need not be the columns chosen with aoe and lq.

Several events

eventdisplay(l200) returns a display without an event, which lplot! fills. The layout is built for the first event and filled in place for the next ones, which is faster than a new figure per event. It is built again for an event with other channels, another LAr configuration, or other waveform panels: another number of traces in a panel, other waveform columns or another legend.

d = eventdisplay(l200)
lplot!(d, evts[1])
lplot!(d, evts[2])

This event has two triggered HPGe detectors, so the table holds two lines per column and both of their strings are in the geometric cut. lplot!(d, ts) takes the time of an event as well, with the keyword event_tier = :jlevt.

The figure holds one event at a time, so save it before the next call:

d = eventdisplay(l200)
for i in idxs
    save("event_$i.png", lplot!(d, evts[i]), px_per_unit = 1.5)
end

Keywords

All keywords except event_tier are given when the display is created, with any form of eventdisplay or lplot, and hold for all events of the display. event_tier is given with each call that takes a time. A keyword that is not listed here is an error.

Figure

KeywordDefaultEffect
event_tier:jlevtThe tier from which eventdisplay(data, ts) and lplot!(d, ts) read the row of the event. Only these two forms take it.
figsize(1800, 920)The size of a new figure.
figurea new Figure(size = figsize)The figure to draw into. It must be empty, otherwise the call throws an ArgumentError. A new layout clears it.

Observables and light

KeywordDefaultEffect
energy:e_cusp_ctc_calThe column of evt.geds shown per triggered detector and added up in the energy sum. The string in the center of the side view is always that of the largest trig_e_cusp_ctc_cal.
aoe:aoe_sg_classifierThe column of evt.geds for the A/E classifier, shown per triggered detector under its name.
lq:lq80_250025_classifierThe column of evt.geds for the LQ classifier, shown per triggered detector under its name.
lar_energynothingThe SiPM energy type of the light and the triggers, one of the energy_types of the LAr configuration. nothing takes the one named in is_valid_lar, and throws an ArgumentError if that does not name exactly one.
lar_cut:geomThe name of the cut in the LAr configuration shown as the geometric cut: the shaded sector, the blue edges and the two table rows. A name that the configuration does not hold throws an ArgumentError. The event tier needs the columns of the cut, <energy>_spms_<name>_<window>_pe_sum and _multiplicity in ged_spm, and holds them only for a cut with dphi_max below 180° in a barrel, so :all does not work. nothing shows no cut: every SiPM counts as inside and has a blue edge, the shading covers the whole circle, and the bands of the side view and the two table rows are left out.
pe_limitsnothingThe limits (low, high) of the logarithmic color scale in photoelectrons, with low > 0. nothing covers at least 0.5 to 10 PE and widens to the light of the event.

Waveforms

These are the keywords of lplot(data, ts), see Waveforms and events. They do not change the top and side views.

KeywordDefaultEffect
system[:geds, :spms]The systems to draw, as a Symbol or a vector. Dict(:geds => [:waveform_presummed, :waveform_windowed]) also gives the waveform columns. Only :geds and :spms have a default column.
show_empty_tracestrueWith false, only the waveforms of the triggered HPGe detectors and of the SiPMs with light anywhere in their trace, also outside the windows. Other systems keep all their channels. A system without such a channel gets no panel. The number of traces then usually changes from event to event, so a display rarely fills its layout in place.
only_processabletrueOnly the channels marked as processable in the statuses of the run. With false, all channels, and a channel missing from plot_tier is an error.
filterbynothingA predicate on the rows of channelinfo, for example ch -> ch.detstring == 3, or a Dict with a predicate per system. A system left without channels gives a warning and is skipped.
groupnothingThe column of channelinfo that groups the channels, or a Dict with a column per system. true takes the string for HPGe detectors and the barrel for SiPMs, false is no grouping.
color:amplitude, or :group with a group:amplitude colors the channels by the height of their signal, :group by their group with a legend, and :channel one by one with a legend.
explodedfalseOne panel per group, by default per string and per barrel.
ncols3The panels per row with exploded. Each system starts a new row.
plot_tierDataTier(:raw)The tier to read the waveforms from.
subtract_baselinetrueSubtract the FlashCam baseline of the trigger from each waveform.
xunitu"µs"The unit of the time axis.
xlimsnothingThe limits of the time axis in xunit. nothing takes the time range of the germanium waveforms.

For only the waveforms of a system, without the array and the table, use lplot(l200, ts; system = :geds). show_empty_traces has no effect there and gives no error.

Marks

KeywordDefaultEffect
watermarktrueWith false, none of the marks below.
finaltrueWith true, no tag on the waveforms. With false, preliminary and approved decide the tag.
preliminarytrueWith final = false: true gives the tag PRELIMINARY, and false leaves the tag to approved.
approvedfalseWith final = false and preliminary = false: true gives no tag, and false gives the tag INTERNAL USE ONLY.
productiontrueThe name of the data production in the corner of the waveforms: the directory that holds the last file listed in LEGEND_DATA_CONFIG. Nothing is drawn if that variable is not set.

Keywords in use

show_empty_traces = false keeps the traces with a signal. The SiPM panel here holds one trace with a pulse outside the windows.

eventdisplay(l200, evts[1], show_empty_traces = false)

system and exploded act on the waveforms only, and the array stays as it is. Here the HPGe detectors take one panel per string.

eventdisplay(l200, evts[1], system = :geds, exploded = true)

lar_cut = nothing shows no geometric cut, so all SiPMs count as inside, and final = false adds the tag PRELIMINARY.

eventdisplay(l200, evts[1], lar_cut = nothing, final = false)
